MY DREAM CONCERT 🤫

Who said in India people only pay for music concerts and entertainment?

Look at the biggest convention center of the country jam packed with thousands of people, who are there for growth.

India is changing and India wants to grow🫡 

Post 1: Look at the face of this kid on the stage who is living a dream he saw at the age of 19 with no money, no influence and no fancy degree, to deliver a speech in front of fully sold out stadium. 🫣

Post 2: My parents saw me live at a conference for the first time, this proud look on their face is the reason why I am happy crying rn❤️

Post 3: Me looking at all of you, and thanking every god in the world. What have I done right to deserve an audience like yours? 🤍🥺

Post 4: right before my speech dad came backstage to hug me and wish me good luck. (Ofcourse after this jhappi the speech had to be good) 🙇🏻‍♂️

Post 5: Hi! I am Raj Shamani. (please read it like: Yeh sheher mera hai and mei is shehar ka Bajirao Singham)

Post 6: Ofcourse I had to talk about: ‘THREE THINGS’ 😂

Post 7 & 8: Just in my element.

Post 9: My family post speech looks complete, my younger brother, dad & mom along with @rajivtalreja  who’s the big brother I never had who ran to me back stage after the speech to come and validate me that it went well. 🤍 (Later whatsapped me 3 things that I need to improve from next time, because ofcourse he is is the one who is never completely satisfied with my speeches because he wants me to reach the next level) 

Post 10: Stage for me is a holy place, where for me nothing matters apart from ‘how to give maximum value to my audience’, and how to serve people who are giving me the most important time of their lives. ✨

At age 16, I used to go to English classes to learn how to speak English fluently and while sitting in the tuition centre I used to write random dreams at the back of my notebook. 😂 

I had no talent, no background, was not from a big city, did not have good grades to make it to IIT / IIM, and wasn’t even able to speak in English properly but I used to believe that I had ‘shaka-laka boom boom magic) 😂 

29th July 2013 - I wrote in my dairy that I will be on the cover of Forbes magazine, (I and my sisters laughed at this crazy dream)

Age 26 - I made it to Forbes cover and Forbes 30 under 30.😭😭

And at this moment, the teenager in me is screaming at the top of his lungs that 'we made it.'

And today, the big dream has finally hit this boy from a small city -Indore.

This would have never been possible without your love and belief in me.

Truth be told, I started my entrepreneurship journey when I was 16 solely because I wanted to achieve this🤫

But along the line, I have fallen in love with the process of educating and helping 100s and 1000s of people.🥺

Coming from a humble family and city, having big dreams was considered a 'luxury.' But today as I get acknowledged for fulfilling mine, it isn't just me who wins.

This is a win for everyone who doubts themselves for not being talented enough, 
not being rich enough, not being from the big city, not being an IIM/IIT graduate & still continue to believe in their dreams. 

it’s a win for all of them, all of us.❤️

Now that we have this baby home, I am ready to go back to basics and fulfil my duty of building the nation, one day at a time.

P.S. Thank you all from the deepest corner of my heart, each of you that has supported me has a special place in my heart. 😭

- Picture 5 is the back of my diary where I used to write random dreams like ‘start a business, ‘give a speech at IIM’ and ‘It is possible to interview people’ 😂

Some people travel to relax.

Some travel to see famous places.

And then there are people who seem to be drawn towards inconvenience.

Listening to @brindasharma talk about her travels, that pattern kept showing up again and again. Remote islands. Roads that barely felt like roads. Weather turning without warning. Cars breaking down in places where help isn’t exactly around the corner.

None of these stories were told like achievements. If anything, most of them sounded uncomfortable while they were happening.

What was interesting was how casually she spoke about it.

The destination rarely felt like the point.

She talked about driving for hours through places that looked like they belonged on another planet. About reaching locations that most people would never think of visiting. About seeing landscapes that make you realise how small your everyday world actually is.

At some point, the conversation stopped feeling like it was about travel.

It started feeling like it was about curiosity.

The kind that makes someone leave the planned route, take the longer road, or keep going simply because they’re wondering what’s on the other side.

Most of us spend a lot of our lives trying to reduce uncertainty.

Some people seem to come alive because of it.

That difference is probably why two people can stand in the same place and have completely different experiences of the world.

The full conversation will be released today at 9 PM.

Dear You,

Teachers in Schools, Elders in Families and Authorities in Society have always taught us to not be Stupid. We have been warned a thousand times to do whatever is possible but stay away from being Stupid. 

Do we really understand what Stupidity is? Can we all allow ourselves to accept that ‘Being Stupid’ can be a choice? Can’t Stupidity be a desired state of emotion or is it necessary that the tag will have to stay with ones personality forever?
Can we all stop making judgements in our head for a second and cherish the stupidity around? Stupid people, Stupid Signboards, Stupid Jokes and Stupid Posts (Like the one you are reading) Can we forget the notions and principles of Good and Bad, Sanity and Insanity, Sophisticated and ‘not so sophisticated’ and look at a human being being human. Being imperfect, being naïve, being stupid. Can we keep a day for ourselves when we can get rid of our insecurities and fears and anxiety and all the negative monsters which haunt our liberation? Can we be courageous enough to make those monsters understand that we feel the need to be stupid. Can we normalize stupidity? for an hour maybe. 
Can we let stupid people know that we have the potential to admire them. Can we allow the kite of Love that we all carry within to conquer the sky of judgement and spread its arms in the season of Life. Can we really make this possible?

Can we think that 'We shall think of Stupidity else we will end up being stupid'?

Regards,
Someone Stupid

ABOUT THE SPECIAL – BE POSITIVE ❤️🎙️
Be Positive is not just a stand-up comedy special — it’s a journey of love, heartbreak, toxic relationships, rejection, healing, and finding happiness again. This story begins with exciting dates, honeymoon phase moments, awkward romance, and relationship highs… then slowly turns into public fights, red flags, emotional chaos, and heartbreak. The biggest twist? My ex cheated on me with her best friend… married him… and somehow invited me to the wedding. From heartbreak and revenge thoughts to moving on, dating again, facing rejection, and finally learning to enjoy single life — this special is about one simple truth: Love is a journey, not a destination.

This is what autonomy looks like.
When you micromanage the systems - not people!

Everyone works at their own pace, allowing them to deliver their best work!

5 signs that you are richer than many people:
(Save this to come back to on your low days)

1/ There are people in your life who will call you and ask you if everything is fine.

2/ You have the time and opportunity to think about your purpose in life. (The problem of “How will you get your next meal?” is not a concern).

3/ You can say no to things in life.

4/ You have a friend who tells you to text them when you get home.

5/ Most important: You have someone in your life who believes in you more than you.

Now, that is being rich.

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on them.

5. How will you spend your life after marriage? What are the expectations from your family? How will your daily routines be? What will be your living arrangements? What have you thought about your children?

This is an important decision. Don't take it in a hurry.

5 things you need to know about building your reputation.

1. Your reputation increases when you don’t get anything from it. 

How do you respond to pressure? How do you respond to people who don’t have much money? This makes your reputation.

2. If someone calls you Sir or Ma’am, it doesn’t mean they respect you. 

Respect that comes because of authority can be a lie. 
The respect that you get from your behavior is the real respect.

3. People who can’t do anything for you - how do you behave with them? 

That shows how strong your value system is.

4. Your reputation is not what people think about you. 
Your reputation is what people expect from you. 

When you say that you will do something, do it. 
When you say you will return something, return it.

5. Your reputation is built by being dependable. 

If people can trust you, they will trust you.

The first brave step is admitting that what the world calls success isn’t your idea of success.

The second is following your inner voice even when the world tells you to be grateful and stop overthinking.

On your last day, you wouldn’t want to think, “I wish I had the courage to live my life differently.”
Which IIT branch gets the highest salaries?

5 month-long challenges that can change your life.
(Share this with a friend you’ll do these with!)

1. Track what gives you energy, and what drains your energy. It can be work, relationships, news. You have to document everything.

2. Pre-take the small decisions in life. 
What to wear, what to eat, where to eat. 
Don’t waste your time on these.

3. Before sleeping, a one-line gratitude journal. Today, I am very thankful for this.

4. Before buying any non-essential thing, wait for 5 days. And after 5 days, ask yourself if that thing is still as important.

5. The most difficult. This will make you a rockstar. Don’t complain about anything. Because the people who complain, they surrender to the problem.

Which of these will you start?

Everyone deserves a work culture where trust is the standard, not a perk.

People do their best work when they feel trusted, respected, and given clarity.
As simple as that!

Love my team @waricrew ♥️

3 Bollywood characters who taught us a lot (Send this to a friend who reminds you of them).

1. Rancho from 3 Idiots. 

Every person is after exams, ranks, and salary. 

He was just learning. 

When nobody asked in class, he would ask questions. 
Nobody asked for help, but he would help.

2. Arjun from Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara. 

He had money, peace, and happiness, but he was alone. 

When he saw his friends enjoying their freedom, he realized that he was in prison. 
He left his dream life and made his own life.

3. Dr. Khan from Dear Zindagi. 

Never told what to do. It was only after asking many questions, that the answers showed themselves.

Today, we can get anything within minutes - information, food, groceries, clothes, even a date!

But the best things in life take time to be nurtured.

Growth.
Purpose.
Relationships.

Don’t rush what’s meant to be built with care!

Took me a while to pen my thoughts. But I had to write it. I never wanted to believe all the rumours floating from the past few days. But when Virat posted about his retirement, it came as a shock. As Anushka mentioned in her post, we all always believed that he would retire from internationals in whites. But this was something unexpected. The man who gave his everything to revive test cricket, the man who filled up a stadium in a Ranji game walking out with a simple Instagram post was not how it was meant to be 💔

Virat made of us wake up at 5am to watch test cricket. His strength, determination and passion towards test cricket made all of us fall in love with the game again. Nobody can forget the way he took us from number 7 to making us the number 1 team in test cricket. Seeing the test mace in his hand always made us fans feel proud. He always maintained that he will walk away when he feels he is not able to give his 100%, but this is not how it was supposed to be. Not going to question his decision because he knows what is best for him but a farewell in whites is what he deserved for being India's greatest test captain. 

Test Cricket is never going to be the same without its strongest pillar. Whites will never feel the same without him wearing it. From 2012, where he took over the mighty Aussies to his last series against them, there have been so many beautiful memories and victories that will be cherished forever. The numbers will always talk about his greatness but it is his attitude, grit and passion for the game that will last forever.

A regret that I will have lifelong is that I never got a chance to watch him play in the whites in a stadium. But as they say that everything has to come to an end, this was it for Virat in the whites. Thank you, Virat, for all the memories. Test cricket will never be the same without you. The fan in me will no more be excited to watch the game without having you in it. But wishing you all the happiness and peace and may you continue to shine in the ODIs and the IPL.

A fangirl forever! Thank you #269 ❤️ All the love, luck and positivity to you❤️🧿

[Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma, Virushka, Test Cricket]

It took me two days to muster the courage to put up this post. I still remember the day I watched a young Virat win the U-19 world cup and it was fascinating to see a young lad break all the norms and change the face of Indian Cricket. 

I am sure that none of his fans would have thought that one day he will become an integral part of our lives. It is hard to believe that a boy from West Delhi went over to win the hearts of people across the globe and it makes us all proud of his success. But there was always a void that despite winning two POTTs, he did not have a T20 World Cup trophy in his name. But finally seeing that happen after all these years is nothing but sheer joy. The 82 not outs against Aus and Pak will always be memorable. But the one against Pak will always be special because the man was going through a tough phase and to come and play such a knock is something only he could do. We all kept waiting for the big 71st Hundred and who would have thought that it would come in the T20 format! But then this is Virat Kohli whom we are talking about and as Anushka had mentioned, he is indeed God's child and he is truly blessed.

I remember my friend and I discussing before the start of this world cup that this could be his last T20 World Cup and last T20I series for India. And I remember I was so happy when we won the finals and he was announced the MoM too. But all hell broke loose the moment he announced that he was retiring from the shortest format of the game. Despite having an inkling about it, hearing it from his mouth and letting that feeling sink in was a very tough pill to swallow. It feels like not only him, but we all grew along with him and it is not just him retiring from the shortest format of the game but a part of us leaving us too. It will not be easy to watch a T20 game without him being there. But everything has to come to an end and so be it. The finals were a bittersweet moment but it gives so much joy to see him the trophy.

Virat, thank you for all the memories in T20 Cricket. The game will not be the same without you. And lastly, you will always be my captain.

Love always,
ND.
